children: New Delhi, Nov. 17 -- After plunging 13% in the previous session, the sell-off inKaynes Technology showed no signs of easing, with the electronics manufacturing services (EMS) major falling another 4% in Tuesday's trade on November 17 to Rs.3,845 apiece. This extended its earnings-led decline for a second consecutive session.

The Street was disappointed with Kaynes Technology's performance in the September quarter, which was impacted by the scale-down of its smart-metering business. The company reported several weak operating metrics.
Not only did its profit after tax decline 62% year-on-year (YoY), but gross debt also increased to Rs.1,810 crore, while working capital days rose to 225 from 210.

Its commitment to refrain from raising funds over the next 12 months also raised concerns, as this could either require a curtailment of capex or greater reliance on debt, potentially putting further pressure on its profit and loss (P&L), said domestic brokerage firm JM Financial.

The weak performance not only weighed on investor sentiment and prompted brokerages to reassess their outlook on the stock. JM Financial cut its target price to Rs.3,050 from Rs.3,850 and retained its Reduce rating.

Jefferies also lowered its target price on Kaynes Technology to Rs.3,625 per share, implying an upside of approximately 22% from Monday's closing price of Rs.2,980. The brokerage said the company's Q2 FY27 performance had sharply missed estimates, prompting it to lower its earnings forecasts for FY27-FY29.
Motilal Oswal, however, reiterated its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs.3,820, based on 30 times its December 2027 estimated earnings per share (EPS).

The brokerage cut its FY27 and FY28 earnings estimates by 28% and 22%, respectively, factoring in the muted quarterly performance and lower earnings expectations across the core EMS, OSAT, PCB, and smart-metering businesses.

Kaynes Technology's consolidated revenue grew 4% YoY to Rs.950 crore, with EBITDA declining 16% to Rs.130 crore. Its EBITDA margin has contracted sharply by 320 basis points to 13.2%, compared with the estimated 15.5%. Adjusted PAT fell 62% YoY to Rs.45.4 crore, against the estimated Rs.79.9 crore.

Revenue from the smart-metering business was deliberately moderated to repair the balance sheet. It fell 80% YoY to Rs.54 crore from Rs.230 crore a year earlier, while revenue for the first half of FY27 stood at around Rs.270 crore. However, the order book remained robust at Rs.10,600 crore as of September 2026, up 30% YoY.

Motilal Oswal said Kaynes Technology's planned exit from Advanced Metering Infrastructure Service Provider (AMISP) operations and its continued focus on reducing smart-metering receivables are expected to improve working capital management and cash conversion. These measures could support the company's target of turning cash-positive by the end of FY27.
Jefferies also echoed a similar view, noting that the company's efforts to reduce its exposure to the smart-metering business could help improve receivables and ease working capital pressures.
